(CNN) -- Cristiano Ronaldo missed an early penalty as Manchester United earned a 0-0 draw in the first leg of the Champions League semifinal at Barcelona's Nou Camp stadium on Wednesday night. Cristiano Ronaldo sent his penalty attempt wide as United failed to take an early lead at the Nou Camp. The Portugal winger, the top scorer in this season's competition, spurned the chance to net for the 39th time overall this campaign and give United a vital away goal. The 23-year-old hit the stanchion high outside goalkeeper Victor Valdes' left-hand post in the third minute after Gabriel Milito handled his header from a Paul Scholes corner. It was United's best chance in a game dominated by the home side, who had the best of possession with some silky moves but failed to find the killer pass in the final third of the pitch. United goalkeeper Edwin van der Sar made a string of saves, especially in the second half, but was not often seriously tested. Barcelona were boosted by the return of Argentina forward Lionel Messi, who started alongside Samuel Eto'o up front, with Thierry Henry on the bench after also being cleared following an illness. Messi picked out Samuel Eto'o in the 13th minute only for midfielder Scholes -- making his 100th Champions League appearance -- to make a vital interception. Barcelona pressed forward again in the 21st minute and Rafael Marquez got clear of his marker but his header failed to trouble Van der Sar, who was back in the side following a groin injury. Then Yaya Toure showed good skill for the home side and sent a good cross into the area that was turned away by Van der Sar. Ronaldo felt he should have had another penalty in the 30th minute when he was bundled over by Marquez after Xavi had carelessly lost possession, but Swiss referee Massimo Busacca allowed play to continue. Eto'o rattled in a shot after 34 minutes but Wes Brown -- who passed a late fitness test to replace the ill Nemanja Vidic in central defense -- made a vital block. Brown partnered Rio Ferdinand, with England midfielder Owen Hargreaves operating as a makeshift right-back. Deco, starting his first game for Barcelona after two months out with injuries, then failed to test Van der Sar with a free-kick in the 38th minute. Marquez was booked in the 44th minute after tripping Ronaldo as he attempted to surge forward, meaning the Mexican is suspended for next Tuesday's second leg at Old Trafford. Ronaldo sent his effort from an acute angle wide of the post. After the break, Messi saw his effort blocked in the 47th minute and then Van der Sar tipped over defender Gianluca Zambrotta's long-range effort. Messi beat three United players but Ferdinand cut out his low cross from the right, then he played in a superb ball for Eto'o -- who lashed his shot against the side-netting. Deco tested Van der Sar with a low drive, then the Dutchman easily dealt with a 20-yard effort from Xavi. Barcelona coach Frank Rijkaard took off Messi in the 62nd minute, replacing him with teenager Bojan Krkic, who scored the winner in the first leg of the quarterfinal against Schalke. A foul on the Serbian-born Spaniard drew a yellow card for Hargreaves in the 73rd minute, then United boss Alex Ferguson bolstered his midfield by bringing on Nani for England forward Wayne Rooney -- who had started up front with Carlos Tevez. Rijkaard responded by replacing Deco with Henry in the 77th minute, and the French forward forced a scrambled save by Van der Sar with a long-range shot on 83. Ferguson brought on veteran winger Ryan Giggs for Tevez soon after, then Van der Sar denied Andres Iniesta and also dived to comfortably save Henry's free-kick from 35 yards. Barcelona continued to press until the final whistle, but still could not create a clear-cut opportunity. E-mail to a friend .

# Manchester United and Barcelona Play to Scoreless Draw in Champions League Semifinal Opener

**(CNN)** -- A missed penalty by Cristiano Ronaldo proved costly as Manchester United could only manage a goalless stalemate against Barcelona in Wednesday's first-leg Champions League semifinal clash at the Nou Camp.

The competition's leading scorer saw his spot-kick sail wide, denying United an early advantage and squandering an opportunity to notch his 39th goal of the season while securing a crucial away goal. The mishap occurred just three minutes into the match, after Gabriel Milito had handled Ronaldo's header—stemming from a Paul Scholes corner—inside the box. The 23-year-old's shot flew high past the left post of goalkeeper Victor Valdes.

That penalty represented United's clearest opening in a contest largely controlled by the Catalan hosts, who dominated ball possession and produced flowing football but couldn't unlock United's defense with a decisive final pass. At the other end, United custodian Edwin van der Sar was called into action repeatedly—particularly after the interval—though none of Barcelona's efforts truly stretched him.

Barcelona's attack received a lift with Lionel Messi's comeback, as the Argentine paired with Samuel Eto'o in attack while Thierry Henry, also recovering from illness, took a spot on the bench. In the 13th minute, Messi threaded a pass to Eto'o, but Scholes—playing his landmark 100th Champions League match—stepped in with a crucial interception.

Barcelona continued pushing forward, and in the 21st minute Rafael Marquez broke free from his defender, though his headed attempt didn't seriously challenge Van der Sar, who had returned to the lineup after recovering from a groin problem. Shortly after, Yaya Toure displayed some fine footwork before delivering a dangerous cross that Van der Sar managed to clear.

Ronaldo believed he'd earned a second penalty in the 30th minute after being knocked down by Marquez following a loose touch from Xavi, but Swiss official Massimo Busacca waved away the appeal. Eto'o then fired a shot in the 34th minute that was crucially blocked by Wes Brown, who had come through a late fitness check to fill in for the ailing Nemanja Vidic at center-back. Brown lined up alongside Rio Ferdinand, while Owen Hargreaves filled in at right-back in an unfamiliar role.

Deco, making his return to Barcelona's starting XI after a two-month injury layoff, failed to trouble Van der Sar with a free-kick attempt in the 38th minute. Marquez picked up a caution in the 44th minute for fouling Ronaldo during a forward run—a booking that rules him out of next Tuesday's return leg at Old Trafford due to suspension. Ronaldo's own follow-up attempt from a tight angle drifted wide.

Following the restart, Messi had a shot blocked in the 47th minute, and Van der Sar tipped a long-distance Gianluca Zambrotta strike over the crossbar. Messi then dribbled past three defenders before Ferdinand intercepted his low delivery from the flank; moments later, Messi set up Eto'o with an excellent pass, but the Cameroonian's shot struck the side netting.

Deco forced a save from Van der Sar with a low shot, and the United keeper easily handled a 20-yard attempt from Xavi soon after. Barcelona manager Frank Rijkaard substituted Messi in the 62nd minute for young talent Bojan Krkic, who had scored the winning goal in the quarterfinal first leg versus Schalke.

Hargreaves received a yellow card in the 73rd minute for fouling the Spanish teenager, prompting United manager Alex Ferguson to strengthen his midfield by introducing Nani in place of Wayne Rooney, who had partnered Carlos Tevez upfront. Rijkaard countered by swapping Deco for Henry in the 77th minute, and the Frenchman nearly scored with a long-range effort in the 83rd minute that Van der Sar scrambled to save.

Ferguson then brought on experienced winger Ryan Giggs for Tevez, while Van der Sar continued his solid display by stopping an attempt from Andres Iniesta and diving to save a 35-yard free-kick from Henry. Barcelona kept applying pressure through the final whistle but were unable to carve out a genuine scoring chance.

The visiting goalkeeper produced the save of the match in the 61st minute, palming away a curling effort that appeared destined for the top corner, tipping it over the bar with fingertip precision.

Not to be outdone, the home side's keeper responded with a smart low save in the 73rd minute, diving to his right to smother a low, driven shot from just inside the area after the visitors broke quickly on the counterattack.

## Tactical Adjustments Shift Momentum

Both managers turned to their benches in search of a breakthrough. The home side introduced a pacy winger just after the hour mark, hoping to inject fresh energy down the flanks, while the visitors countered by bringing on an additional holding midfielder to shore up their defensive shape and slow the game's tempo.

A late substitution saw the home team's captain withdrawn in the 82nd minute, seemingly as a precaution after appearing to favor his hamstring following a sprint — a concerning sign for the second leg given his importance to the side going forward.

## Looking Ahead

Despite the lack of goals, both managers expressed cautious optimism heading into next week's decisive second leg.

"A clean sheet away from home in a semifinal is not a bad result," the visiting manager noted. "We showed character, we created moments, and now we go home knowing anything is possible."
